title: Bosonic codes from compact phase spaces
authors: David Roberts, Aaron Slipper, Alireza Parhizkar, Victor V. Albert, Mohammad Hafezi
abstract: We present the algebraic structure of bosonic quantum error-correcting codes on genus-two Riemann surfaces. We explicitly construct the code words as automorphic forms and analytically generate the full tower of code spaces at all weights. We prove a fundamental no-go theorem: for any genus greater than one, the stabilizer group is non-amenable, forcing a strictly positive spectral gap in the stabilizer Hamiltonian. Consequently, no normalizable quantum state can satisfy all stabilizer conditions. This sharply contrasts with standard Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes, where the amenability of the stabilizer group $\mathbb{Z}^2$ permits approximate code words with arbitrary precision.
summary: This paper establishes a rigorous mathematical boundary for bosonic quantum error correction codes based on the geometry of their phase space. It proves that for surfaces of genus two or higher, the underlying group structure is non-amenable, which mathematically forces a spectral gap that prevents the existence of any stable, normalizable code state. This contrasts sharply with the well-understood case of the torus.
main_problem: The paper investigates the algebraic structure and existence of bosonic quantum error-correcting codes defined on compact Riemann surfaces of genus $g \geq 2$. The core problem is determining when such codes can support normalizable quantum states.
main_result: A fundamental no-go theorem is proven: for genus $g \geq 2$, the non-amenability of the surface group forces a strictly positive spectral gap in the stabilizer Hamiltonian, precluding the existence of any normalizable code state.
method: The authors use tools from algebraic geometry (automorphic forms, Riemann-Roch theorem) combined with quantum information theory concepts like stabilizer codes and spectral gap analysis.
model_or_system: The system models bosonic quantum error correction on a phase space defined by a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma_g$. The code space is defined by states fixed by the action of the surface's fundamental group $\Gamma$.
key_observables: Spectral Gap ($\delta$), Amenability of the stabilizer group ($\Gamma$), Dimension of the code space ($\dim H_\Gamma$).
important_parameters: Genus ($g$), Stellar Rank ($r$), The structure of the surface group $\pi_1(\Sigma_g)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the uniformization theorem and the mathematical framework connecting quantum states to global sections of line bundles on the Riemann surface.
figures_summary: Figures compare the spectral gap ($\delta$) for $g=1$ (Torus/GKP, $\delta=0$) versus $g=2$ (Bolza surface, $\delta>0$), illustrating the physical consequence of group amenability.
paper_structure: The paper contrasts the known case of $g=1$ (amenable group, allowing approximate codes) with the general case $g \geq 2$. It develops the no-go theorem by linking the non-amenability of the surface group to a positive spectral gap, which mathematically forbids exact or approximate code states.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep geometric constraint on quantum error correction, showing that the topology of the underlying physical space (the Riemann surface) dictates the fundamental feasibility of encoding quantum information.
